@ssahani  I don't know if I miss some fundamentally from the RFC's but I think you mixed up the concepts of DHCP Options in general and the specific DHCP option "Vendor Specific Information".

The former is the generic concept to add any option the DHCP protocol and consists of a code (1-254) and opaque data:
E.g. `Code=73` and `Data=10.0.0.42 10.0.0.44` (maybe with `DataType=ipv4address`) would produce the "Default Finger Server Option" (RFC 2132 8.18.).

The latter is the specific "Vendor Specific Information" option described in RFC 2132 8.4. with code 43 and one (or multiple !) opaque data strings, see:

> The Encapsulated vendor-specific options field SHOULD be encoded as a
>    sequence of code/length/value fields of identical syntax to the DHCP
>    options field with the following exceptions:
> [..]


The encoding of the latter might look similar to the encoding of generic options but is not mandatory (_SHOULD be encoded_), e.g. it is possible to send a simple string. Because of this, I propose to leave this special encoding to user, so they have to use a byte sequence in the config file including the Zero-Byte, Length and 255-Byte. If you know how to use this "custom option", you are able to use the specific encoding your opposide software needs.

To conclude, if you want to implement both in this Pull Request, you have to split it into two parts:
(1) a `VendorSpecificInformation=` config (maybe multiple config options to support both string value and byte sequence) in both `[DHCPv4]` and `[DHCPServer]`, as this option can be used by client and server.
(2) two new sections (also for both client and server) to allow generic options with your proposed `Type=`, `Data=` and `DataType=`. Additionally `Type=` is a bad name, as this is always called "code" in the standards.

@flo-wer I am referring to 
https://tomsalmon.eu/2017/02/isc-dhcp-server-option-43-vendor-specific-attribute/

```
The DHCP server will return the Vendor attributes in the DHCP Response. The data returned is encoded in binary in the following format for each code:
Byte 0: code
Byte 1: length
Byte 2: data
…
Byte length+2: final data byte
… then follows the next field, starting with code, length, data…
```
